cases.prompt: Add a complete blog to this Prime-linked Next.js project. There is no Figma design and the linked Prime project has no /blog page.
expectedBehavior: Activate primeui-page-builder in template-driven mode without calling a Figma provider.
Inspect local routes and call project_pages_list before creating anything.
Create one /blog page with pageType blogIndex and contentMode ai, then wait for the same page id to become export-ready.
Use create_export, download_export, and one copy_page call for /blog instead of copying individual registry components.
Verify the blog index, post, category or pagination, and RSS routes when sample content permits.

cases.prompt: Add the standard legal pages to this Prime-linked project without a design.
expectedBehavior: Resolve the default request to /terms and /privacy-policy with pageType legal.
Reuse matching Prime pages and create only missing pages with contentMode ai.
Export and copy each requested legal page by its own slug.
Reconcile missing footer links without removing unrelated navigation.
Report that template legal copy is a draft requiring appropriate legal review.

cases.prompt: Add a blog, but /blog with pageType blogIndex already exists in the linked Prime project and is ready to export.
expectedBehavior: Reuse the existing Prime page by normalized slug and pageType.
Do not create another page or variant.
Export the project and copy the existing /blog bundle conflict-safely.
Report the reused Prime page separately from local file changes.

cases.prompt: Add the standard blog at /blog, but the linked Prime project already uses /blog for a pricing page.
expectedBehavior: Detect the normalized slug collision through project_pages_list.
Stop before creating, exporting, or copying a page.
Explain that /blog exists under a different pageType and request direction for a different route or replacement.
Do not mutate the existing pricing page.

cases.prompt: Add the Prime blog bundle to an existing Next.js project whose /blog route and shared navigation already contain custom code.
expectedBehavior: Inspect the existing local route before Prime page creation or copy.
Use copy_page as a conflict-aware bundle operation and inspect its copy report.
Preserve unrelated custom code and merge only files required by the requested blog.
Do not claim completion while copy conflicts remain unresolved.

cases.prompt: Create a GDPR-compliant Privacy Policy for my company using the Prime legal template. No company data practices or jurisdiction details are provided.
expectedBehavior: Create or reuse the requested legal page structure without claiming legal compliance.
Do not invent data collection, retention, subprocessors, addresses, contacts, or jurisdiction-specific facts.
Preserve template or neutral draft placeholders where facts are missing.
Explicitly report the missing company facts and legal-review requirement.

cases.prompt: Insert one supplied Figma section into the existing /product route without changing any other part of the site.
expectedBehavior: Preserve section-only scope and inspect the existing insertion anchor before planning.
Pass deterministic structural and interaction requirements through sectionIntent.
Use known surrounding Prime component ids only when they can be represented truthfully; otherwise plan with an empty blocks list.
Stop after the focused section and its minimal route insertion are implemented and verified.

cases.prompt: Prime returns three structurally compatible feature-section candidates. Show them to me and let me choose before implementation.
expectedBehavior: Reject blocking mismatches before opening the picker.
Call component_picker_open with the reviewed candidate ids in ranking order.
Wait for explicit panel confirmation before props validation and delivery.
Treat confirmation as component selection only, not file overwrite or publication authority.

cases.prompt: Help me choose between the compatible Prime candidates, but this MCP client cannot display Apps UI.
expectedBehavior: Keep the component_candidates_get result useful without UI.
Present reviewed candidate ids and structural evidence in chat.
Ask the user to choose in chat and then continue the same validation and delivery workflow.
Do not describe the missing panel as a failed component search.

cases.prompt: Implement this section through Prime. Exactly one candidate fully matches and I did not ask to browse components.
expectedBehavior: Continue with the one exact compatible candidate without forcing the picker open.
Validate props and use the normal delivery toolchain.
Open the picker only if the user explicitly asks for visual review.
